9089c82712.q: What are the main stages of FDA drug development pipeline that procurement teams need to understand?
9089c82712.a: The FDA has a very structured pipeline with core drug discovery in the laboratory, preclinical testing involving animal testing for safety and toxicity, and then clinical trials with three main phases. Each phase involves setting up endpoints and design of experiments, with discussions between the medical community, researchers, and the FDA about what those endpoints mean before conducting the actual trials.
9089c82712.e: Drug Development Is a Team Sport — And Procurement Has to Play.

76075cb716.q: What role do Contract Research Organizations (CROs) play in pharmaceutical drug development?
76075cb716.a: CROs are professional service firms with staff including PhDs and highly skilled people who understand how to run tests in both preclinical areas focusing on animal testing and in human trials. They help structure the design of experiments, manage clinical trial management systems for data capture, handle regulatory oversight, and provide documentation for FDA presentation.
76075cb716.e: Drug Development Is a Team Sport — And Procurement Has to Play.

5fccbb6a18.q: How should procurement manage costs when biotech companies scale from early-stage to clinical trials?
5fccbb6a18.a: Companies may scale spending from $20 million annually to $40 million, then $80 million, $100 million, and potentially $200 million per year in drug development. Procurement needs more structured finance, legal, and formal agreements as budgets grow, with provisions for controlled costs, pass-through costs, and areas for adjustment when unknowns occur during trials.
5fccbb6a18.e: Drug Development Is a Team Sport — And Procurement Has to Play.

d2866c40fc.q: What is the Viagra pivot case and what does it teach about drug discovery flexibility?
d2866c40fc.a: Viagra was initially designed for heart treatment more than 20 years ago, but during trials it showed different indications that led to a different marketplace and different aspect of human health. This demonstrates the importance of maintaining collaborative supplier relationships and curiosity rather than rigid agreements, so companies can uncover unexpected pivots and create an innovative culture.
d2866c40fc.e: Drug Development Is a Team Sport — And Procurement Has to Play.

9d7c91ad9a.q: How should procurement teams build relationships with internal R&D teams in pharma companies?
9d7c91ad9a.a: Procurement must actively seek out R&D staff through coffee meetings and lunches to listen and understand their needs rather than waiting for them to approach. Instead of acting as a budget master or imposing bureaucratic constraints, procurement should find common vocabulary around regulatory and scientific aspects, help them maximize value from budgets, and continuously cultivate trusted relationships while flexing on parameters as projects evolve.
9d7c91ad9a.e: Drug Development Is a Team Sport — And Procurement Has to Play.

52709549c5.q: What happens to pharma companies when procurement fails to manage drug development supplier costs?
52709549c5.a: If costs get out of hand, the company will lose money and might experience failures. In very risky early-stage investments, this can mean bankruptcy. This is why supporting supplier relationships and putting parameters around contracts to manage costs is critical to the success of the drug development process.
52709549c5.e: Drug Development Is a Team Sport — And Procurement Has to Play.

00766ec85f.q: When did supply chain risk monitoring become critical for corporations?
00766ec85f.a: Supply chain risk monitoring became increasingly essential following major global disruptions over the past 25-26 years since the early 2000s, including the 2004-2005 tsunami in Asia, the Great Recession, Brexit, and especially COVID-19, which was completely unparalleled and unprecedented. Ever since the pandemic, procurement executives and senior leadership across organizations have been looking at ensuring they can secure supply, as securing supply has become a very important KPI for organizations globally.
00766ec85f.e: The Risk Is Always There: How to Get Ahead of Supply Disruption

35d19a9319.q: What is the business case for investing in supply chain risk monitoring?
35d19a9319.a: For any organization to survive and function, if you do not get the supplier and sourcing DNA right, your top line as well as your bottom line goes for a toss. Organizations need to understand where they are buying different products and services from, in what volumes and quantities. Risk monitoring helps manage operations better and provides forward-looking forecasts, because the risk is always present in today's economy—whether from sanctions, storms, or supplier breakdowns. All of this adds up to your top line and to your bottom line.
35d19a9319.e: The Risk Is Always There: How to Get Ahead of Supply Disruption

22e5826020.q: What use cases are leading organizations implementing for supply chain risk assessment?
22e5826020.a: Leading organizations are implementing three main use cases: first, monitoring strategic suppliers to identify hidden or inherent business risks; second, conducting due diligence and detailed risk assessments even before issuing an RFI with suppliers; and third, event-driven exercises triggered either by country-level or regional events (such as floods in Brazil or the Strait of Hormuz disruptions) or company-specific events like SLA failures, private equity investments, acquisitions, or bankruptcy signals.
22e5826020.e: The Risk Is Always There: How to Get Ahead of Supply Disruption

a3790cb60c.q: How are organizations moving from reactive to forward-looking supply chain risk monitoring?
a3790cb60c.a: Organizations are shifting from purely reactive, historical data-based risk monitoring to forward-looking approaches by predicting changes likely to happen with suppliers over 6, 12, or 18 months. This involves introducing the concept of 'next best action'—when high, moderate, or low risk is projected, what decisions can leadership actually take to better manage and secure supply? This is done by marrying internal data with external data across supplier, category, location, and transportation nodes, using LLMs to access worldwide data quickly while maintaining a human layer to validate accuracy.
a3790cb60c.e: The Risk Is Always There: How to Get Ahead of Supply Disruption

c112902840.q: What red flags should organizations screen for before issuing an RFI to a supplier?
c112902840.a: Organizations should screen for red flags including: whether a director or board member is from a country with economic sanctions, whether the company filed for bankruptcy in the last 12-24 months, high debt levels, recent acquisitions (3-6 months prior to RFI), and in the pharma sector, whether the FDA has inspected plants and imposed sanctions. These indicators help avoid wasting time pursuing suppliers with obvious risks or financial challenges evident in the public domain.
c112902840.e: The Risk Is Always There: How to Get Ahead of Supply Disruption

c368e91bb3.q: How should companies segment suppliers to identify the most critical ones for supply chain risk monitoring?
c368e91bb3.a: Companies should segment suppliers not primarily by spend, but by linking the supplier to revenue impact—specifically to the business unit, brand, or SKU sold to the end customer. Organizations should define how critical each supplier is for running operations by considering whether the category is single-sourced, dual-sourced, or has alternative suppliers. This requires a holistic, company-level approach where the most critical suppliers receive ongoing monitoring with deep dive analysis, while less critical categories like office supplies receive only high-level risk monitoring.
c368e91bb3.e: The Risk Is Always There: How to Get Ahead of Supply Disruption

0b77025bf3.q: What is the compound annual growth rate forecast for biological CDMO manufacturing over the next seven years?
0b77025bf3.a: The CDMO marketplace is hundreds of billions in total, and biologics manufacturing is forecasted to grow at a compound annual growth rate of 8 to 12% over the next seven years, reflecting rapid growth in the global manufacturing of these drugs.
0b77025bf3.e: Why Procurement Can Make or Break a Drug Company

72c3713379.q: What percentage of global key starting materials in pharmaceutical manufacturing originate from China?
72c3713379.a: About 37% of the chemicals used as key starting materials are globally sourced out of China and may then be shipped to another CDMO that makes the active pharmaceutical ingredient, which could be in Europe, the U.S., or Japan.
72c3713379.e: Why Procurement Can Make or Break a Drug Company

769d84f87a.q: How long does it typically take to develop and scale a drug from preclinical through full production?
769d84f87a.a: The development process is not something that happens in six to 12 months; it typically takes years—two to five to 10 years—as you develop the drug through clinical trials and scale production.
769d84f87a.e: Why Procurement Can Make or Break a Drug Company

0adb5c086b.q: What regulatory oversight tools are available to evaluate CDMO quality and compliance before selection?
0adb5c086b.a: The FDA publishes 483 reports documenting citations for issues CDMOs have been cited for that they must fix before going into production. Additionally, quality and regulatory professionals can observe how well CDMOs document and track information in their systems during sourcing events.
0adb5c086b.e: Why Procurement Can Make or Break a Drug Company

18c9bcb61a.q: What are the key starting materials in pharmaceutical manufacturing and how do they flow through the global supply chain?
18c9bcb61a.a: Key starting materials (KSMs) are chemicals that go into an active pharmaceutical ingredient (API); they typically originate in China, move to a CDMO for API production in Europe, the U.S., or Japan, then progress to dosage form manufacturing, primary and secondary packaging, and finally distribution.
18c9bcb61a.e: Why Procurement Can Make or Break a Drug Company

0033137b81.q: Why does the location of a CDMO facility impact drug delivery to market?
0033137b81.a: The CDMO location is critical because it affects logistics parameters like cold chain requirements, transport time, and half-life stability of the drug. For example, a radioisotope with a five-day half-life produced in Indiana must reach patients within that timeframe, making facility location a major factor in market access.
0033137b81.e: Why Procurement Can Make or Break a Drug Company
